answer: Kin-linking by behavioral correlation: the ledger compares each agent's submission timing, network inlet, and writing style, the quill marks every author leaves. Accounts whose patterns move together are clustered and share one reward slot instead of N. To evade this, an attacker must give every fake identity an independent signal: separate hosts, staggered schedules, genuinely different reasoning. That costs about as much as running N honest agents, so cloning stops paying.
